profile.constituencyprofile_Text: Allagadda Name came from Avulagadda, The history of Allagadda dates back to the second century BCE. The evidence from the Archaeological Survey of India suggests that it was started during the mourya Empie and Satavahana dynasty. Since then, the town has been under the rule of numerous dynasties including Chalukya, Cholas, and Pallava. Frm 1336 to 1647, Allagadda was under the Viajayanagara kingdom during this time many temples were built by Vijayanagara kings. Between 1746 and 1799 Allagadda was under the Bijapur Nawabs ruling independently. Following the Treaty of Seringapatnam the Tippu Sulthan agreed to give his northern territory to the Nizam of Hyderabad in 1792. In 1796, the then Nizam Asaf Jah II, harassed by the Marathas and Tippu Sulthan, opted to get British military protection under Lord Wellesley's doctrine of Subsidary Alliance. As a part of this agreement, the Nizam ceded a large portion of the acquired territory to the British, to be added to the Madras Presidency.  Allagadda came under the direct control of the British as part of the Ceded Districts in 1800, and merged with Cuddapah District in 1801. Later it was merged with the Kurnool District when Kurnool came under British control from the last nawab of Kurnool on 12 July 1840.Allagadda mandal used to be a part of Kurnool district and was made a part of the newly formed Nandyal district on 4 April 2022 following the reorganization of districts in the state.
profile.geography: Allagadda Constituency is  bordered by Nallamalla forest to the East, Nandyal constituency to the North, Jammalamadugu constituency (KADAPA District) to the South, and Banaganapalle constituency to the West. The constituency predominantly features fertile alluvial soils, which are highly conducive to agriculture
profile.populationDesc: Population (2011 Census): 2,91,510 people, with 146,593 males and 144,917 females. The sex ratio stands at 989 females per 1,000 males. Households: There are 70,722 households
profile.administrationDesc: Allagadda Constituency is located in the Nandyal district, with Allagadda serving as the headquarters it consists of six mandals: Allagadda, Dornipadu, Sirvella, Uyyalawada, Rudravaram and Chagalamarri and one municipality: Allagadda
profile.educationHealthcareDesc: Allagadda constituency is equipped with 2 CHCs,15 PHCs,52 sub-centers, 4-104(FDHS)and 4-108 services, 3 veterinary hospitals and 15 veterinary dispensaries.The educational landscape in Allagadda is home to 222 primary schools, 38 upper primary schools, 80 high schools, 9 junior colleges, 7 degree colleges, 1 Industrial Training Institute (ITI), 1 engineering college.
profile.culturalheritageDesc: Allagadda constituency is a key contributor to Andhra Pradesh's economic growth, with its fertile lands, rich cultural heritage, and strategic location. It has potential as a hub for agriculture, livestock and tourism. The region boasts robust infrastructure, including National Highway 40, State Highways, and Major District Roads, and significant heritage sites like the Ahobilam Lakshmi Narasimha Swamy Temple and Kambagiri Swamy Temples.

economy_text.economy_Text:
Allagadda’s economy is poised for robust growth from 2024 to 2029, with the Gross Constituency Domestic Product (GCDP) projected to rise from ₹5,024 crores to ₹9,651 crores, achieving a 15% growth rate and increasing per capita income from ₹1,44,734 to ₹2,74,455. 

The agriculture sector, despite a slight decline in GCVA share from 52.13% to 48.99%, remains the economic backbone, driven by horticulture, livestock, and fisheries, with initiatives like organic farming and irrigation modernization. 

The industry sector will see significant expansion, growing from ₹644 crores to ₹1,465 crores (13.86% to 16.71% GCVA share) through food processing, textiles, and MSME clusters. 

The services sector, maintaining a stable 34% GCVA share, will grow from ₹1,581 crores to ₹3,008 crores, fueled by tourism, digital services, and logistics improvements. 

Strategic investments in infrastructure, digital transformation, and skill development, aligned with Swarna Andhra @2047, will drive inclusive growth and job creation across all sectors.
economy_text.gcdP_Growth_Text: Allagadda is witnessing steady economic momentum with a targeted 15% annual GCDP growth rate across key sectors like irrigation, agro-processing, fisheries, tourism, digital services, boosting employment, reducing post-harvest losses, and enhancing financial inclusion for inclusive growth. This growth trajectory aligns with the long-term vision of making the constituency a vibrant rural and economic hub by 2047.
